note.note:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P)

History:
• Chief complaint: Burning/stinging pain with urination, increased urinary frequency, and lower abdominal (“bottom of tummy”) ache for just under one week.  
• Course: Gradual onset; pain worst while voiding. Frequency significant enough to disrupt university activities.  
• Hematuria: Noted pink-tinged urine today; no frank red blood previously.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, flank/back pain, or new bowel changes. No abnormal vaginal discharge.  
• Gynecologic/sexual: Last menstrual period ~2 weeks ago; sexually active with long-term boyfriend; unprotected intercourse ~1 week ago; on combined oral contraceptive. No current concern for pregnancy raised by patient.  
• Triggers/relievers: None reported; has not tried analgesics prior to call.  
• Similar episodes: First occurrence.  

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).  
• No known renal or bladder disorders.  

Allergies:
• Clindamycin – adverse reaction (details not documented).

Medications:
• Combined oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Mebeverine – dose/route/frequency not documented (for IBS).

Physical Examination:
• Virtual encounter; no physical exam performed.  
• Patient reports no fever; no flank or costovertebral angle pain.  
• Mental status: Alert, oriented, conversant.  
• Other systems: Not recorded.

Impression:
Acute uncomplicated cystitis (urinary tract infection) – based on classic triad of dysuria, frequency, suprapubic discomfort, and mild hematuria without systemic features.

Differential (consistent with transcript):
1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis – most likely (see above).  
2. Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis – possible given unprotected intercourse; lacks discharge or pelvic pain.  
3. Distal ureteric/bladder stone – less likely; absence of colicky flank pain.

Management Plan:
• Antibiotic therapy: Offer 3-day course of Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim (specific drug/dose pending final prescribing decision).  
• Diagnostic test: Mid-stream urine (MSU) sample to be dropped off at practice today for dipstick and culture; results to guide/confirm antibiotic choice.  
• Symptomatic care: Encourage liberal oral hydration; use Paracetamol as needed for discomfort (dose not documented).  
• Safety-net advice: Return or call if fever, back/flank pain, vomiting, or worsening symptoms occur; otherwise follow up if no improvement within one week.  
• Lifestyle: Advised against further cannabis use for general health.  
• Contraception: Continues combined pill; no change advised.  

Patient Summary:
19-year-old female with first episode of dysuria, frequency, suprapubic ache, and pink urine for <1 week; presentation most consistent with uncomplicated cystitis. Urine culture arranged and empiric short-course antibiotic started; patient counselled on hydration, analgesia, and red-flag symptoms.

Key Takeaways:
• Start prescribed 3-day antibiotic course today and complete fully.  
• Drink plenty of water; take Paracetamol if needed.  
• Seek prompt medical review if fever, back pain, vomiting, or no improvement by next week.

Next Steps:
• Submit urine sample today; clinic will contact patient with culture results.  
• Telephone or in-person review in 7 days if symptoms persist or sooner if red-flag symptoms develop.
